 FILE — The early voting location in West Hartford in 2024. 
 Democrats continued to build up a lead in early voting turnout, although the margin shrank somewhat on Wednesday, the third of 14 days of early voting in Connecticut.
 Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas’ office reported Thursday morning that 32,640 voters cast a ballot on Wednesday, bringing the total number of early votes so far to 112,977. In addition, 27,8563 voters had returned an absentee ballot, for a grand total of 140,830 votes so far.
 Among those who cast a ballot Wednesday, 16,872 were registered Democrats, compared to 9,895 unaffiliated and minor party voters and 5,873 Republicans. Over the first three days of early voting, Democrats had cast 62,555 ballots. Unaffiliated and minor party voters had cast 31,656 and Republicans 18,766.
 Of the absentee ballots, collected so far, 14,486 have been cast by Democrats, 8,172 by unaffiliated and minor party voters and 5,235 by Republicans. These numbers are subject to change as not all towns report on the same schedule.
 West Hartford continues to lead the state in early voting, with 2,406 residents casting in-person votes. Milford, (2,185), Stratford (2,148), Fairfield (2,078) and Norwalk (2,051) round out the top 5.
 Early voting continues through Nov. 1, with Election Day on Nov. 3.
